Tolerance = 0.01 + 0.01*|ref| ≈ 0.01 + 0.01*|x|. For error > tolerance: 0.01*|x| > 0.01 + 0.01*|x| → 0 > 0.01, which is impossible. The 1% perturbation is exactly absorbed by the 1% rtol.

For any input x, the error is bounded by ~0.01*|output| while tolerance is 0.01 + 0.01*|output|, so error can never exceed tolerance mathematically. The atol=1e-2 provides a floor that the small multiplicative error cannot overcome. For large |x|, both original and mutant approximations diverge from tanh(x) similarly, keeping their difference small.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant appears mathematically unkillable with atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2 tolerances. The 1% constant perturbation produces ~1% output error which is exactly absorbed by 1% rtol. To kill this mutant would require tighter tolerances (e.g., rtol=1e-3) or exploiting numerical instability which does not appear present.
rounds.recommendations: When designing tolerance thresholds for mutation testing, ensure rtol is strictly less than the smallest constant perturbation percentage you want to detect. A 1% constant perturbation requires rtol < 0.01 to be reliably detected.
